steps.note: One step: the time out, the departure confirmed, and the pass returned or outstanding, together.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. No open visit, a time out before the time in, a visit already closed, a pass belonging to another visit, or an outstanding pass with no reason closes nothing.
plan.atomicity: One write: the visit closed with the departure **confirmed** (BR-5), and the pass either freed for the next visitor or held outstanding as a credential still in circulation (BR-3). Nothing is deleted (BR-6).

operations.name: visit.log.out
operations.idempotencyKey: visit_id, since a visit is closed once (BR-8)
operations.purpose: Close an open visit with the time out, and account for its pass.

parameters.name: visit_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open visit at this branch matches that pass or name (E1). Nothing is closed.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the open visits that match with their pass numbers and times in.

parameters.notes: The open visit, found by the pass number returned or by the visitor's name — a visitor at the desk will have one or the other (BR-7, A3).

parameters.name: time_out
parameters.notes: When the visitor left, as the desk says. After the time in (E2).

parameters.name: pass_returned
parameters.notes: Whether the numbered pass came back (BR-3). Stated by the desk, never assumed.

parameters.name: outstanding_reason
parameters.notes: Up to 250 characters, the desk's own words. Required where the pass did not come back (E5).

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The staff member acting. Never from the request.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The closed visit and where its pass stands.

fields.name: pass_number
fields.description: The pass that went out on this visit.

fields.name: pass_state
fields.description: Returned and free to issue again, or Outstanding — a credential still in circulation, which cannot be reissued (BR-3, AC-3).

fields.name: hours_on_site
fields.description: How long the visit was open.

errors.meaning: No open visit matches the pass or the name.
The time out is before the time in.
The visit has already been closed.
The pass was issued to a different visit.
The pass did not come back and no reason was given.

planningRules.rule: Never assume the pass came back. Returned frees it for the next visitor; outstanding keeps it out of circulation. A pass marked returned that is still in a visitor's pocket is a credential nobody is chasing (BR-3).
Never write the outstanding reason. Where the pass did not come back the desk says why, and without a reason nothing is recorded (BR-3, E5).
Never supply the time out. It is when the visitor left, as the desk says — not when the request was typed (BR-2, E2).
Never reopen a closed visit. A visitor found on site after the closure is logged in again as a new visit (E6).

reversal.statement: A closed visit is never reopened (E6), and a closure is never deleted (BR-6). A visitor still on site after closure is logged in again with visit.log.in — UC-29-01.

routesElsewhere.note: A closed visit is not reopened. A visitor found on site after the closure is logged in again, so the record stays honest (E6).

steps.note: One step. Each named open visit is closed with its departure unconfirmed (BR-4).

plan.atomicity: One write per visit, in one call: each closed **unconfirmed**, and each pass that did not come back recorded outstanding (BR-3, BR-4). Nothing is deleted; the unconfirmed closure is itself the record that a visitor was not seen leaving (BR-6).

operations.name: visit.close.unconfirmed
operations.idempotencyKey: visit_ids, since each visit is closed once
operations.purpose: Close named open visits with the departure unconfirmed.

parameters.name: visit_ids

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open visit at this branch matches.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the open visits that match with their pass numbers, times in and hours on site.

parameters.notes: The open visits being closed — named one by one, or every visit still open at this branch where the desk says all of them.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The staff member acting. Never from the request.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What was closed and which passes are now outstanding.

fields.name: closed
fields.description: Each visit closed, with its time in and hours on site.

fields.name: passes_now_outstanding
fields.description: Passes that did not come back with these visits — each recorded outstanding (BR-3).

fields.name: still_open
fields.description: Visits at this branch still open after this call.

errors.meaning: A named visit has already been closed.

planningRules.rule: Say these read unconfirmed. Closing a visit is not watching somebody leave, and the unconfirmed closure is the record that a visitor was not seen leaving (BR-5, BR-6).
Never close a visit this way when the desk watched the visitor leave — that departure is logged out, confirmed (BR-2, BR-5).
Report the passes now outstanding. A visitor who never signed out still has the pass, and an unreturned pass is a credential in circulation (BR-3, BR-9).
Say that the end of the day is not defined. Nothing sets when open visits are closed, so the close happens when the desk does it (OQ-1).

reversal.statement: An unconfirmed closure is not reopened. A visitor found on site afterwards is logged in again as a new visit, so the record stays honest (E6).

operations.name: visitor.pass.recover
operations.idempotencyKey: pass_id, since a recovery is the same state however often it is recorded

parameters.name: pass_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No outstanding pass at this branch carries that number.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the matching outstanding passes with the visit each went out on.

parameters.notes: The pass, named by its number.

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The staff member acting. Never from the request.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: state
fields.description: Returned, and free to issue again (BR-3, AC-9).

errors.meaning: The pass is not outstanding — it is free, issued to an open visit, or retired.
errors.note: The lifecycle takes only an outstanding pass back to returned (A4), and the use case writes no exception for the attempt.

planningRules.rule: Only an outstanding pass is recovered this way. One still issued to an open visit comes back with that visit's log-out (BR-3, A4).
Never bring back a retired pass. Retired is final (BR-9, E8).

reversal.statement: A recovery is not undone. If the pass goes missing again it goes out on a visit, and is recorded outstanding again when that visit closes without it (BR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: V-014 is returned and free to issue again.

plan.atomicity: One state change: outstanding to retired, which is terminal (BR-9).

operations.name: visitor.pass.retire
operations.idempotencyKey: pass_id, since a pass is retired once
operations.purpose: Retire an outstanding pass that was never recovered.

parameters.name: pass_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No outstanding pass at this branch carries that number. Only an outstanding pass is retired.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the matching outstanding passes with the visit each went out on.

parameters.notes: The pass, named by its number.

parameters.name: retire_reason
parameters.notes: Why it is being retired, in the School Admin's words (BR-9).

parameters.name: staff_id
parameters.notes: The staff member acting. Never from the request.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: state
fields.description: Retired. Terminal — the number is never issued again (BR-9, E8).

fields.name: days_outstanding
fields.description: How long it was out before it was retired.

errors.meaning: The pass is not outstanding — it is free or issued to an open visit.
errors.note: The lifecycle retires only an outstanding pass, and the use case writes no exception for retiring one that is free or issued.

planningRules.rule: Say it is final. A retired number is never issued again, and nothing brings it back (BR-9, E8).
Say that nothing sets when a pass should be retired. How many days outstanding is too many is not decided, so the School Admin is choosing (OQ-2).

reversal.statement: A retired pass is never brought back. Retired is terminal, and a retired number is refused if issued (BR-9, E8).
